title: 7.1.14 Your Turn: Build a Sprite
description: Low-stakes autograded practice. Instantiate the Sprite class twice (rectangle form and circle form), set properties on each instance, and give one sprite a stroke. Bridges the 7.1.7 / 7.1.13 worked examples and the 7.2.11 Enemy class worked example.

steps.title: Create the canvas
steps.instructions: In `setup()`, create a canvas. `Canvas` is a class, and `new Canvas(...)` stamps out an instance: the same constructor-call pattern you saw in 7.1.7.
hints: Open the moSHion docs drawer on the right and find the Canvas section.

steps.title: Instantiate a rectangle sprite
steps.instructions: Store a new rectangle sprite in a variable, using the 4-argument constructor form `new Sprite(x, y, width, height)`. Then set its `.color`.
hints: Check the Sprite section of the moSHion docs drawer for the 4-argument constructor form.

steps.title: Instantiate a circle sprite
steps.instructions: Store a second sprite using the 3-argument constructor form `new Sprite(x, y, diameter)`. With one size instead of a width and a height, moSHion makes a circle, that many pixels across. Give this instance its own `.color` (different from the first, so you can tell them apart).
hints: Check the Sprite section of the moSHion docs drawer for the 3-argument constructor form.

steps.title: Give one sprite a stroke
steps.instructions: Pick either sprite and set its `.stroke` AND its `.strokeWeight`. These are two more properties every sprite has: `.stroke` is the color of its outline, a color string just like `.color`, and `.strokeWeight` is how thick that outline is, in pixels (for example `s.stroke = 'yellow';` then `s.strokeWeight = 4;`). You'll see a visible outline on that sprite.
hints: Look up sprite properties in the moSHion docs drawer.

requirements.title: Canvas created with a size
requirements.description: Creates the canvas with explicit dimensions rather than leaving the placeholder

requirements.title: Rectangle sprite (4-arg form)
requirements.description: At least one `new Sprite(x, y, w, h)` call with four arguments (a fifth body-type argument such as 'static' is fine). Help: 5.1.6 (Sprite: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) + .color)

requirements.title: Circle sprite (3-arg form)
requirements.description: At least one `new Sprite(x, y, diameter)` call with exactly three arguments. Help: step 3 of this lab.

requirements.title: Property set on an instance
requirements.description: At least one `.color` assignment on a sprite instance. Help: 7.1.3 (Class and instance)

requirements.title: Stroke used
requirements.description: A `.stroke` or `.strokeWeight` property is assigned. Help: step 4 of this lab.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "7.1.14 Your Turn: Build a Sprite". The task they were given: Starting from an empty setup(): create a canvas with new Canvas(width, height); store a rectangle sprite made with the 4-argument form new Sprite(x, y, width, height) in a variable and set its .color; store a circle sprite made with the 3-argument form new Sprite(x, y, diameter) and give it its own .color; then give one of the two sprites a .stroke and a .strokeWeight. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. new Sprite(x, y, w, h) makes a rectangle; new Sprite(x, y, d), with one size, makes a circle d pixels across. A fifth argument such as 'static' only sets the body type, so it is still the rectangle form. sprite.stroke is the outline colour and sprite.strokeWeight its thickness in pixels. A plain stroke(...) or strokeWeight(...) call is a drawing setting, not a property of a sprite. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, ternaries or if-chains, semicolons, spacing, quotes, order and helper functions of their own are all fine; only a name the starter's own code already calls or reads has to keep that name. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or a string never runs, so the starter's STEP comments are never the student's work. Any numbers, expressions (such as width / 2) or variables work as arguments. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise. Write for a 14-year-old beginner: short sentences and everyday words.

rubric.title: Canvas created with a size
rubric.description: setup() calls new Canvas(...) with a width and a height (numbers, expressions or variables). Missing: no canvas.

rubric.title: Rectangle sprite (4-arg form)
rubric.description: At least one new Sprite(...) given x, y, a width and a height (four values). A fifth body-type argument such as 'static' still makes a rectangle and counts. Missing: no sprite with both a width and a height. Help: 5.1.6 (Sprite: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) + .color)

rubric.title: Circle sprite (3-arg form)
rubric.description: At least one new Sprite(...) given exactly three values: x, y and a diameter. Missing: no three-value sprite. Help: step 3 of this lab.

rubric.title: Property set on an instance
rubric.description: At least one sprite's .color is assigned with =. Missing: no .color is set on a sprite. Help: 7.1.3 (Class and instance)

rubric.title: Stroke used
rubric.description: A sprite's .stroke or .strokeWeight is assigned with =. Setting both is what step 4 asks and is welcome. A plain stroke(...) function call does not set a sprite's property. Missing: neither property is set on a sprite. Help: step 4 of this lab.
